subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction and memoryFlush work from foreground same-session message handling, and what transcript-ordering contract should that design preserve?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the fix changes scheduler, session-state, transcript rotation, cancellation, and channel-delivery semantics rather than a narrow line repair.

options.title: Isolate compaction lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency lane or worker so foreground user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for the full maintenance timeout.

options.title: Keep serialization and add recovery
options.body: Keep the current same-lane model but add a shorter bounded failure path plus visible busy or retry recovery so users are not silently blocked.

options.title: Preserve blocking behavior
options.body: Treat compaction as intentionally foreground and close or defer nonblocking message handling as out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Isolate compaction lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency lane or worker so foreground user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for the full maintenance timeout.
